interface.title: METABRIC Survival Dashboard (Streamlit demonstrator)
interface.field: Clinical oncology / breast cancer survival epidemiology and biomedical machine learning
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis and communicating results (educational demonstrator, not a clinical decision tool)
interface.what_it_is_for: Browse cohort summary numbers for the METABRIC breast cancer cohort, compare Kaplan-Meier survival curves across clinical subgroups, and get a 5-year mortality risk from a pre-trained Random Forest for a hypothetical patient profile.

data.note: The seeded data/ files give a synthetic cohort of only 30 patients, not METABRIC. Every count, percentage and log-rank p-value read from the charts in this tree comes from that synthetic cohort and is not a METABRIC result. The donut tooltips show ER+ 16 and ER− 14, and the KM legends show n=16/14, 9/11/10 and so on. The Home KPI cards are fixed values from the full study (1,904 patients, 57.9% event rate, 154 months median survival, ROC-AUC 0.69), so they disagree with the seeded charts. The ER caption says '~77% ER+' while the donut shows 53.3%. On the Survival page, the caption under each chart quotes p-values from the full study (p=0.02 for ER, 2.22e-05 for HER2, 7.45e-05 for PR). The chart titles show log-rank p-values from the seeded data instead (1.23e-07, 9.18e-08, 3.91e-04). The ML Prediction page uses the bundled rf_model.joblib.

features.name: Stratified Kaplan-Meier viewer with log-rank test
features.general: Pick a grouping variable and see time-to-event curves per group, with confidence bands, group sizes, a significance test and an interpretive note
features.specific: Stratification variable dropdown (ER, HER2, PR, Histologic Grade, Chemotherapy, Hormone Therapy) drives a Plotly KM chart. The title shows the log-rank p only for two-group variables (none for the three-group Histologic Grade). The legend shows n per group, and a caption sits below. In this run the curves, n and title p come from the synthetic 30-patient data, while the captions quote full-study p-values.
steps: Open the Stratification variable dropdown
Choose a variable (two-group or three-group)
Read the curves and CI bands and the n per group in the legend
For two-group variables, read the log-rank p in the title
Read the interpretation caption beneath
serves_tasks: Compare survival curves and a significance test for one grouping variable, and read the accompanying interpretation

features.name: Interactive survival-curve inspection
features.general: Inspect a multi-series chart closely: read values on hover, zoom to a time window, hide a series, pan, reset and export an image
features.specific: Standard Plotly modebar and legend controls on the KM chart (framework behaviour, not tool-specific): hover tooltip (time, survival), box zoom, legend toggle, pan, Reset axes, and Download plot as a PNG. Hiding a group leaves its CI band visible.
steps: Hover a curve to read (months, survival probability)
Drag a box to zoom into a time range
Click a legend entry to hide that group
Pan or reset the axes
Download the view as a PNG
serves_tasks: Look closely at part of the curves

features.name: Patient profile form with live risk card and baseline gauge
features.general: Fill in a case's attributes with sliders, radios, dropdowns and checkboxes. A trained classifier's probability updates at once and is shown against a population baseline, with colour coding for above or below the baseline.
features.specific: The Clinical profile, Biomarkers and Treatments inputs feed the Random Forest. The Result card shows the % and 'Above/Below cohort-average mortality risk' in red or green. The 5-Year Mortality Risk gauge has a white marker at the ~22% cohort rate.
steps: Set age, tumor size, positive lymph nodes and mutation count with the sliders (drag or Home/End keys)
Choose histologic grade from the dropdown
Set ER/PR/HER2 radios and tick treatments
Read the predicted % and the above/below label on the result card
Compare the gauge needle with the white ~22% baseline marker
serves_tasks: Read the model's estimate for a default profile and compare it with the cohort baseline
Enter a hypothetical case's characteristics and get a risk estimate
Vary inputs to see how sensitive the estimate is

features.name: Global feature-importance bar chart
features.general: Show the top predictors of a trained model as a ranked horizontal bar chart, with exact values on hover
features.specific: 'Top 5 factors (global model)': numeric__lymph_nodes_examined_positive, numeric__tumor_size, genomic__mapt, numeric__age_at_diagnosis, genomic__flt3
steps: Scroll to Top 5 factors
Read the ranking
Hover a bar to read its importance value
serves_tasks: See which inputs the model relies on most

features.name: Cohort KPI cards with category donut
features.general: Summarise a dataset with headline metric cards and a part-of-whole chart whose categories can be hovered and toggled
features.specific: Home KPI cards (Patients, Event rate, Median survival, ROC-AUC) are fixed full-study text, not computed from the loaded data. Beside them, an ER Status donut is drawn from the loaded (here synthetic 30-patient) data, with tooltip counts and a legend toggle.
steps: Read the KPI cards (fixed values)
Hover a donut slice for its count and %
Click a legend entry to hide a category
serves_tasks: Inspect how the cohort splits on a key marker
